title: Boiling Point of Water
hint: Think about the definition of the Celsius temperature scale. What two points define it?
prompt: Water boils at 100°C (212°F) at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.

feedback.correct: Correct! At sea level with standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm), water boils at exactly 100°C (212°F). This is actually the definition of the Celsius scale - 0°C for freezing, 100°C for boiling.
feedback.incorrect: Actually, this statement is true. Water boils at 100°C at sea level. Perhaps you were thinking of water at high altitudes, where it boils at lower temperatures due to reduced atmospheric pressure?
